_provenance.citation: Catalano C, Scuoppo R, Turgut T, Bouwman V, Gotzen N, Cannata S, Gentile G, Gandolfo C, Pasta S. Credibility assessment of patient-specific modeling in transcatheter aortic valve implantation. I. A population-based validation of patient-specific modeling. APL Bioeng. 2025;9(4):046101.
_provenance.model: patient-specific finite-element and FSI model of SAPIEN 3 Ultra TAVI deployment
_provenance.not_a_per_factor_assessment: 3 of 13 V&V 40 factor names present, zero 'credibility factor', zero 'gradation'. The paper says so itself: 'the ASME also recommends an applicability assessment to complete the credibility assessment. This was, however, not carried out in this study.' It exercises the modelRiskLevel and hasContextOfUse rows only, and must NOT be scored for factor routing.
_provenance.recovered_by: Discarded from the corpus for a ~10% inter-word space-loss extraction fault, which turned out to be one pdfplumber parameter (x_tolerance=1.2, 9.98% -> 0.02%). The rejection conflated 'unusable for factor routing' with 'unusable'.
_provenance.erratum_unverified: A PMC search reported errata for both TAVI papers in 2026. Crossref shows no update-to relation on this record and the erratum was not retrieved. Whether it touches the risk statements transcribed below is UNKNOWN. Check before quoting this bundle's levels.

decision_consequence.span: the decision consequence was deemed significant since the in silico model output may yield erroneous predictions, potentially causing serious harm to patients when applied in clinical contexts

model_influence.span: the model influence was deemed significant, as the model is designed to assess the performance of TAVI devices of varying sizes and hemodynamic conditions on a certain subject to guide regulatory decisions

model_risk.span: the model was designated a risk rating of 5 on a 1-5 scale, suggesting the necessity for high credibility goals

credibility_goal.span: the comparison of the quantity of interest between the comparator (i.e., the clinical data) and the computational model is predicated on differences of less than 5%

_k8_adversarial: A SECOND kind of deviation, distinct from Bologna's. Bologna substitutes an input NAME -- regulatory impact for model influence. This paper keeps both V&V 40 input names but gives them a value the standard does not define ('significant' rather than a gradation), and reports the result on a 1-5 numeric scale that V&V 40 also does not define. So a K8 validator cannot index the standard's table here either, and must report not_derivable with the substituted values named -- for a different reason than Bologna. Two documents, two deviations, neither of which is an error to normalise away.
